Definition: from ἄγαν (much) and G242; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:--be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).
BiblicalUsage: Agalliao is to jump for joy — exulting, rejoicing greatly. Jesus tells the persecuted to rejoice and be exceeding glad; Mary says her spirit hath rejoiced in God her Saviour; Abraham rejoiced to see Christ's day; and Peter says believers rejoice with joy unspeakable, even though they do not see Him now. The word is always joy that cannot stay still — it leaps.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the sound of real faith. Joy in Christ is not a quiet politeness; it jumps, it exults, it sings — and even suffering cannot keep it down, because the joy is in Him, not in the circumstances.
RelatedTopics: Joy; Joy in hardship; Praise; Worship
